joymoti_konwari.ref_desc: Joymoti Konwari is a late‑20s Assamese noblewoman with an oval medium‑brown face, calm resolute eyes, long black hair in a low bun with a wooden pin, wearing cream and pale‑gold muga mekhela‑chador with maroon borders, leaf‑green blouse, red‑white sash, and carrying a dark bamboo staff.

jayadhwaj_singha_and_the_rajshal_mint_gu.display_name: Jayadhwaj Singha of the Rajshal Mint
jayadhwaj_singha_and_the_rajshal_mint_gu.figure: Jayadhwaj Singha and the Rajshal mint guilds
jayadhwaj_singha_and_the_rajshal_mint_gu.ref_desc: Jayadhwaj Singha is a sturdy, medium-brown Assamese king with a black topknot, off‑white angarkha, deep-maroon waistcoat, cream dhoti, white-and-red gamosa stole, modest gold jewellery, and he always holds a wooden coin-die block and short iron hammer in a warm off‑white, maroon, cream and golden-beige palette.

rudra_singha_and_pramatta_singha.display_name: Rudra Singha & Pramatta Singha of Rang Ghar
rudra_singha_and_pramatta_singha.ref_desc: Rudra Singha and Pramatta Singha are medium-brown Assamese Ahom kings with black hair in cloth-tied knots, wearing mustard-gold and sage-green knee-length jamas over white dhotis with cream/red shawls, Rudra bearing a sheathed curved dao and Pramatta holding a manuscript and small clay Rang Ghar roof model, in a mustard-gold, sage-green, cream, white and brick-red palette.

rajeswar_singha_and_the_chang_rung_phuka.figure: Rajeswar Singha and the Chang-Rung Phukan
rajeswar_singha_and_the_chang_rung_phuka.ref_desc: Rajeswar Singha is a tall medium-brown Assamese king with a topknot wrapped in a white band, maroon knee-length tunic, cream dhoti, off-white red-bordered shawl, gold belt and a sheathed straight dao, beside the lean Chang-Rung Phukan in indigo tunic, plain dhoti, beige shawl, carrying a palm-leaf manuscript and wooden measuring rod, all in maroon, cream, off-white, indigo and brown tones.

srimanta_sankaradeva_and_madhavdeva.ref_desc: Srimanta Sankaradeva is a wiry, grey-haired Assamese elder with a small topknot under a flat off-white turban, off-white long tunic, cream-bordered dhoti, cream gamosa, tulsi necklace and wooden staff holding a wrapped palm-leaf manuscript, always beside Madhavdeva, a lean, clean-shaven Assamese man in an off-white tunic, pale-cream dhoti with maroon border, cream gamosa, off-white turban and a light-brown khol drum at his hip with a slim stick, both in muted off-whites, creams, maroons and light browns.

the_chang_rung_phukan_and_rudra_singha.figure: The Chang-Rung Phukan and Rudra Singha
the_chang_rung_phukan_and_rudra_singha.ref_desc: Chang-Rung Phukan and Rudra Singha appear together: light-brown complexions, sharp almond-eyed faces, black hair in cloth-wrapped topknots, the architect-priest in off-white tunic, mustard-gold dhoti and green-striped shawl with bamboo measuring staff and manuscript, and the king in deep-red silk coat, cream lowers, golden-yellow sash and white muga shawl resting his hand on a sheathed straight Ahom sword, all in Assamese-Ahom colours of off-white, mustard-gold, deep red and golden yellow.

simuka_and_kanha.ref_desc: Simuka and Kanha Satavahana are medium-brown Deccan brothers with oval faces, Simuka’s hair in a high black topknot with a gold circlet and Kanha’s in a lower knot with a red band, wearing off-white and saffron dhoti-uttariya with beige quilted vest and indigo-ochre dhoti-uttariya with grey-blue tunic, brown leather sandals, Simuka carrying a plain curved iron sword at his hip and Kanha a rolled palm-leaf charter, in a palette of off-white, muted saffron, deep indigo, maroon and brown leather.

queen_naganika.ref_desc: Queen Naganika is a medium-brown oval-faced woman in her early 30s with long black hair in a high bun under a thin gold circlet, wearing a deep-red sari with gold border, mustard-gold upper cloth, simple gold jewellery, leather sandals, and carrying a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a red cord.

the_kanaganahalli_sculptors.ref_desc: A lean mid-20s Deccan sculptor with medium-brown skin, black hair in a small back knot with an off-white forehead band, wearing an off-white cotton uttariya and ankle-length dhoti with dull-red borders and wooden sandals, holding a grey limestone relief slab plus iron chisel and wooden mallet in a palette of off-white, dull red, brown, grey and black.

gautami_balashri.ref_desc: Gautami Balashri is a warm medium-brown, late-middle-aged woman with an oval face and calm half-smile, dark hair in a low bun wrapped with a cloth band and a small gold forehead disc, wearing a deep-red mustard-bordered Satavahana-style sari draped modestly over a blouse with simple gold jewellery and bare feet, always holding a rolled palm-leaf manuscript, in a palette of deep red, mustard yellow, off-white, warm brown and dull gold.

satavahana_royal_women.ref_desc: Satavahana Royal Patroness with an oval medium-brown face, large dark eyes, black hair in a high bun with gold band, turmeric yellow sari with maroon border over maroon blouse, gold jewellery, and a grey inscribed stone donation tablet, accented with indigo details.

the_jogalthambi_hoard.ref_desc: A slim, medium-brown young guardian with an oval face, high-knot black hair with side locks, off-white tunic, reddish-brown dhoti, mustard-yellow belt, dull-green shoulder shawl, simple silver jewellery, brown sandals, a grey coin-pouch, and a bronze tray of overstruck silver coins with one coin held up.

satavahana_moneyers.ref_desc: A mid-30s Deccan moneyer with medium-brown skin, dark topknot and white headband, wearing off-white angavastra and terracotta dhoti with dark-indigo sash, copper ornaments and sandals, holding a wooden minting tray of lead, potin and copper coins plus stone anvil and iron punch in off-white, terracotta, indigo, lead grey and copper tones.

deccan_cave_engineers.ref_desc: A mid-30s lean Deccan cave engineer with medium-brown skin, black hair in a short back knot and red headband, wearing an off-white wrap tunic, light-brown dhoti, indigo sash, ochre shawl and sandals, always carrying a notched wooden measuring staff with a bronze plumb bob.

satavahana_administrators.ref_desc: Śivakhaṇḍila is a lean, medium-brown Satavāhana administrator with an oval face, trimmed beard, black hair in a low knot wrapped by an off-white band, wearing an off-white shawl, cream tunic, indigo dhoti, maroon sash, simple gold ornaments, brown sandals, and holding a rolled palm-leaf charter with a bronze seal.

the_periplus_merchant.ref_desc: The Periplus Merchant is a lean, sun-tanned Greek-speaking trader in an off-white knee-length linen tunic with purple-brown borders, light beige himation cloak, tan leggings, dark brown sandals, dark brown mid-neck wavy hair with an off-white headband, and he always carries a rolled waxed-wood writing tablet with stylus, accented by a dark red belt and simple bronze ring.

satavahana_scribes.ref_desc: Satavahana Prakrit Scribe with medium-brown oval face, black hair in a low knot with white headband, off-white wrapped upper cloth and ankle-length dhoti, deep-ochre waistband, brown sandals, copper armlet, holding a stone inscription slab with chisel and wooden mallet.

gunadhya.ref_desc: Guṇāḍhya is a mid-30s lean medium-brown man with an oval face, short beard, black hair in a topknot with a white headband, wearing an off-white shawl over a pale-ochre tunic, off-white trousers, dark-brown sandals, beaded mala, and carrying a red-bound palm-leaf manuscript and stylus in off-white, pale ochre, dark brown, dark red, and black tones.

the_satavahana_successors.ref_desc: A medium-brown Deccan noble in an off‑white tunic, saffron‑orange shawl, deep green ankle‑length dhoti and brown sandals, with black hair in a braided topknot, gold circlet and simple jewellery, carrying a leaf-bladed straight sword in a brown scabbard, in a gold‑green‑saffron palette.

mayurasharma.ref_desc: Mayurasharma appears as a lean, medium-brown young man with an oval face, dark intense eyes, a sandalwood tilak, long dark hair in a Brahmin topknot with a thin gold headband, wearing an off-white dhoti with deep maroon border, pale yellow tunic, cream maroon-bordered shawl, simple sandals, sacred thread and minimal gold-rudraksha jewellery, carrying a plain iron sword with leather-wrapped hilt in a brown scabbard, all dominated by off-white, deep maroon, pale yellow, brown leather and gold colours.

banavasi.ref_desc: Banavasi appears as a lean medium-brown teen boy with an oval face, black hair in a small top-knot with an ochre headband, wearing an off-white dhoti, cream shawl and dull-red vest with dark-green belt and copper ornaments, carrying a bound palm-leaf manuscript roll.

kakusthavarma.ref_desc: Kakusthavarma of Banavasi is a medium-tall, early-40s Deccan king with a medium-brown complexion, oval face, short beard, black hair in a high topknot held by a gold headband, wearing an off-white angarkha, golden-ochre dhoti, deep-maroon uttariya, gold jewellery and Jain pendant, brown sandals, and carrying a straight double-edged sword in a deep-brown scabbard with red-and-gold baldric as his signature weapon, in a palette of deep maroon, golden ochre, off-white, warm brown and gold.

santivarma.ref_desc: Santivarma Kadamba is a mid-20s medium-brown Deccan prince with a high black topknot, tilaka, off-white tunic, deep-green uttariya with three gold medallions, mustard-gold dhoti, simple gold jewellery, brown sandals, and a plain sheathed iron sword at his left hip.

mrigeshavarma_and_ravivarma.ref_desc: Mrigeshavarma and Ravivarma are a father–son pair with medium-brown oval faces and black topknots under simple gold circlets, wearing cream tunics, deep-red or teal uttariyas and mustard/light-ochre dhotis with gold jewellery, the father gripping a plain iron sword and the son holding a rolled copper-plate charter, all in deep red, mustard yellow, muted teal, cream and gold tones.

harivarma_and_krishnavarma_ii.display_name: Harivarma & Krishnavarma II of the Kadambas
harivarma_and_krishnavarma_ii.ref_desc: Two medium-brown Deccan princes stand together: Harivarma in deep-maroon dhoti, cream tunic and golden-yellow uttariya with low-knot dark-brown hair and gold headband, Krishnavarma II in forest-green dhoti, beige vest, sky-blue uttariya, black topknot with bronze circlet, sharing one red-sheathed curved sword at Krishnavarma’s hip.

halmidi_inscription.ref_desc: A lean, medium-brown young male scribe with sharp black eyes, black hair in a short topknot and white headband, wearing an off-white long-sleeved tunic, dull-ochre dhoti with dark-green border, pale-cream uttariya, simple copper jewellery, and holding a grey stone inscription-slab and slim iron chisel.

kubja.ref_desc: Kubja of Talagunda is a medium-brown, oval-faced Sanskrit poet with a short beard, dark hair in a neat back knot with a white headband, wearing off-white dhoti and uttariya with a pale saffron scarf and copper bangle, holding a palm-leaf manuscript bundle with stylus.

kadamba_shikhara.ref_desc: Kadamba Shikhara is a medium-brown, oval-faced young man with large focused eyes, black hair in a low bun with an off-white headband, wearing an off-white angavastra, dull-ochre dhoti with dark-red border, simple beads and bangles, barefoot, carrying a wooden stepped-shikhara model and small tools in warm earthy colours.

chandravalli_archaeology.ref_desc: A lean late-20s Deccan trader with medium-brown skin, short black topknot and off-white headband, wearing an off-white angarkha, mustard-yellow shawl, deep-indigo dhoti with reddish-brown border, brown sandals, minimal bronze jewellery, and carrying a brown leather-slung cylindrical coin pouch showing mixed coins and a palm-leaf strip.

mayurasharma_s_land_grants.ref_desc: A mid-30s Deccan Brahmin patron with medium-brown skin, high black topknot, off-white dhoti and uttariya with mustard-yellow border, light-brown wrap, minimal gold jewellery, and a bundled palm-leaf and copper-plate land-grant case in off-white, mustard, light-brown, dark-red and bronze tones.

kadamba_patrons.ref_desc: A medium-brown, oval-faced Kadamba king in his mid-30s with a high black hair bun and gold circlet, off-white angavastra, deep red ankle-length dhoti with gold border, gold jewellery, brown sandals, and a copper land-grant plate bundle with red cord and stylus.

yaduraya_wodeyar.ref_desc: Yaduraya Wodeyar is a mid-30s lean brown-complexioned man with an oval face, neat moustache, black hair in a low knot under a deep-red bordered turban, wearing a white angarakha, dark-indigo sleeveless vest, off-white dhoti, off-white shawl, minimal gold jewellery, and a simple talwar at his left hip in a brown scabbard, in a palette of white, off-white, deep red, dark indigo, and brown.

raja_wodeyar_i.ref_desc: Raja Wodeyar I has an oval medium-brown face with sharp dark eyes, a short moustache, and black hair in a low bun under a deep maroon gold-trimmed turban, wearing a maroon patterned jama, cream churidar trousers, olive green sleeveless war-vest, gold waistband, brown mojari shoes, light gold jewellery, and carrying a plain brown-sheathed south Indian steel sword at his left hip.

kanthirava_narasaraja_i.ref_desc: Kanthirava Narasaraja I is a medium‑brown, strong‑jawed man in his early forties with a black low‑bun hairstyle under a deep maroon turban, wearing an off‑white angarkha, forest‑green sleeveless quilted coat, beige dhoti, maroon sash, and carrying a curved talwar and a silver Kanthiraya coin in deep maroon, forest green, beige, off‑white and brown tones.

chikka_devaraja_wodeyar.ref_desc: Chikka Devaraja Wodeyar is a wheat-brown, oval-faced Mysore king in a cream angarkha, deep green sleeveless coat, saffron waistband, white dhoti, maroon peta with gold band and feather, wearing simple gold jewellery and brown mojari shoes, carrying a gold-hilted steel talwar in a brown scabbard.

hyder_ali_and_krishnaraja_wodeyar_ii.figure: Hyder Ali and Krishnaraja Wodeyar II
hyder_ali_and_krishnaraja_wodeyar_ii.ref_desc: Hyder Ali is a late-40s, medium-brown, sharp-eyed soldier with a white gold-edged turban, off-white angarkha over deep indigo churidar, dark-green sash and sabre at his hip, beside Krishnaraja Wodeyar II, a slimmer, fairer king in cream-gold angarkha, maroon churidar and dark-red gold-banded turban holding a palm-leaf manuscript.

tipu_sultan.ref_desc: Tipu Sultan is a medium-built, mid-30s man with a rounded medium-brown face, thin moustache, cream Mysore turban with green band and gold crescent badge, wearing an off-white striped angarkha, dark green sash, dark teal sleeveless overcoat, churidar trousers, brown mojari shoes, and a curved gold-hilted sabre with green tassel at his left hip.

krishnaraja_wodeyar_iii.ref_desc: Krishnaraja Wodeyar III is a light-brown-complexioned man of about 30 with an oval face, small moustache, maroon Mysore turban with gold bands and white feather, cream-and-gold striped angarkha, maroon shawl, green waist-belt, off-white churidar, brown mojari shoes, pearl necklace, and a plain brown-sheathed curved ceremonial sword at his left hip with subtle gold fittings and a green-stoned pommel.

krishnaraja_wodeyar_iii_and_chamaraja_wo.display_name: Krishnaraja Wodeyar III & Chamaraja Wodeyar X
krishnaraja_wodeyar_iii_and_chamaraja_wo.figure: Krishnaraja Wodeyar III and Chamaraja Wodeyar X
krishnaraja_wodeyar_iii_and_chamaraja_wo.ref_desc: Two Mysore Wodeyar maharajas stand together: both in cream silk achkans with maroon‑gold stoles, cream‑gold turbans, pearl‑emerald necklaces, cream mojari shoes, and a shared ceremonial gold‑hilted curved sword at Chamaraja’s left hip with Krishnaraja’s hand resting on its pommel.

k_seshadri_iyer_and_krishnaraja_wodeyar_.display_name: K. Seshadri Iyer & Young Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV
k_seshadri_iyer_and_krishnaraja_wodeyar_.figure: K. Seshadri Iyer and Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV
k_seshadri_iyer_and_krishnaraja_wodeyar_.ref_desc: A dignified mid‑50s Seshadri Iyer with maroon Mysore turban, white angarkha, churidar and navy shawl stands beside teenage Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV in dark‑green silk angarkha, red sash and green turban, both holding a rolled Shivanasamudra project map accented in white, maroon, navy, dark green and gold.

m_visvesvaraya_and_krishnaraja_wodeyar_i.display_name: M. Visvesvaraya & Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV (KRS Era)
m_visvesvaraya_and_krishnaraja_wodeyar_i.figure: M. Visvesvaraya and Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV
m_visvesvaraya_and_krishnaraja_wodeyar_i.ref_desc: A medium-brown-skinned duo: white-haired Visvesvaraya in a mid-grey Western suit, white shirt, black tie and white Mysore turban holding a rolled dam blueprint, alongside Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV in an off-white silk angarkha, maroon waist sash, cream churidar, royal turban and gold-capped wooden cane, all in grey, off-white, maroon, black and gold tones.

krishnaraja_wodeyar_iv_and_m_visvesvaray.display_name: Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV & Sir M. Visvesvaraya
krishnaraja_wodeyar_iv_and_m_visvesvaray.figure: Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV and M. Visvesvaraya
krishnaraja_wodeyar_iv_and_m_visvesvaray.ref_desc: Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV and M. Visvesvaraya stand together, with Krishnaraja in an ivory silk achkan, deep-maroon turban and green sash, Visvesvaraya in off-white long-coat, white dhoti and plain white turban, both holding a shared rolled institutional blueprint accented by dark green details.

krishnaraja_wodeyar_iv_and_jayachamaraje.figure: Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV and Jayachamarajendra Wodeyar
krishnaraja_wodeyar_iv_and_jayachamaraje.ref_desc: Two Mysore maharajas stand together, both wheatish oval-faced men with neat moustaches, Krishnaraja in a maroon angarakha, ivory churidar and tall maroon jeweled turban, Jayachamarajendra in a navy bandhgala, cream churidar and cream turban, sharing a brown leather portfolio with gold emblem.

gargi_vachaknavi.ref_desc: Gargi Vachaknavi is a medium-brown, oval-faced woman in her early thirties with sharp dark eyes, long black braided hair with cotton wraps and a simple headband, wearing an off-white wrapped sari and ochre-brown inner tunic with minimal wooden and copper ornaments, carrying a dark brown wooden staff and a small palm-leaf manuscript, in a palette of off-white, muted ochre-brown, dark brown, copper and black.

maitreyi.ref_desc: Maitreyi is a mid-20s, medium-brown skinned woman with an oval face, large thoughtful dark eyes, a sandalwood tilaka, long dark hair in a single mid-back braid with a cloth band and white flowers, wearing an off-white early Vedic sari with dull-indigo border over an ochre-brown inner tunic, simple bronze and thread jewelry, brown sandals, and carrying a bound palm-leaf manuscript bundle with a wooden stylus.

avvaiyar_i.ref_desc: Avvaiyar of Tagadur is a warm medium-brown skinned woman in her late 30s with an oval face, black hair in a low bun with an off-white band, wearing a deep maroon lower drape with mustard border, muted indigo upper cloth, simple gold and bead jewellery, barefoot with a bronze anklet, and carrying a palm-leaf manuscript bundle with a wooden stylus at her belt.

didda_of_kashmir.ref_desc: Queen Didda of Kashmir is a late-30s regal woman with an oval light-brown face, sharp dark eyes, long dark hair in a low bun under a pale-cream headscarf, wearing a deep indigo patterned pheran over madder-red layers with a muted-gold sash, modest gold jewellery, brown boots, and carrying a plain dark-brown scabbarded straight sword at her hip.

chand_bibi.ref_desc: Chand Bibi is a mid-30s, medium-brown Deccan noblewoman with an oval face, large brown eyes, a left-eye beauty mark, dark braided hair under an emerald-green turban, wearing a saffron-gold jamah over off-white kurta and indigo churidar with boots, carrying a brown-hilted tulwar and a red-tied parchment scroll in a palette of saffron-gold, emerald green, deep indigo, off-white and brown leather.

udayamati.ref_desc: Udayamati of Patan is a mid-30s Gujarati queen with an oval medium-brown face, calm focused expression, long black hair in a low braided bun with a gold hairband, wearing a deep maroon cotton-silk sari with dull-gold borders over a gold choli, modest gold jewellery and brown sandals, holding a rolled palm-leaf architectural plan, in a palette of maroon, dull gold, off-white, warm brown and soft stone-grey.

akka_mahadevi.ref_desc: Akka Mahadevi is a slim young woman with medium‑brown skin, long dark braided hair wrapped with thread, wearing an off‑white sari with a maroon border over a dark indigo blouse, simple silver and copper ornaments, a black‑cord lingam pendant, flat sandals, and carrying a palm‑leaf manuscript bundle with stylus.

lal_ded.ref_desc: Lal Ded is a late‑middle‑aged Kashmiri woman with an oval, light brown face, deep brown eyes, dark hair in a low bun under an off‑white headscarf, wearing a dusty‑rose woollen pheran, off‑white layers, simple silver jewellery, and holding a small wooden mala.

savitribai_phule.ref_desc: Savitribai Phule is a medium-brown, oval-faced woman in her mid-30s with intense eyes, hair in a low bun under a deep indigo nauvari sari with red-gold border, maroon blouse, olive shawl, simple silver jewellery and dark sandals, always holding a worn leather-bound lesson book with a wooden slate and stylus.

pandita_ramabai.ref_desc: Pandita Ramabai is a mid-30s light-brown-complexioned woman with an oval face, serious eyes, wavy black hair in a low bun under a white-edged dupatta, wearing a deep indigo cotton sari with maroon border over a high-necked white blouse, minimal gold studs and bangle, brown sandals, a beige shoulder bag, and carrying a brown leather-bound book with papers and a wooden fountain pen in an indigo, maroon, white, warm brown and gold palette.

anandi_gopal_joshi.ref_desc: Anandi Gopal Joshi is a slight, early-twenties Indian woman with an oval medium-brown face, large dark eyes, center-parted black hair in a low bun under an off-white pallu, wearing a deep indigo sari with maroon and gold trim, maroon long-sleeved blouse, simple gold jewellery, dark brown slippers, and holding a worn brown medical textbook with a small brass-handled stethoscope looped around it.

kamala_sohonie.ref_desc: Kamala Sohonie is a mid-1930s Indian biochemist with an oval medium-brown face, large determined dark eyes, black hair in a low bun with a black ribbon, wearing an off-white kurta, dark-navy cardigan, charcoal-grey skirt, off-white dupatta with maroon border, brown Oxford shoes, and carrying a worn brown leather lab notebook and a pale-green-filled glass test tube.

vijayalakshmi_pandit.ref_desc: Vijayalakshmi Pandit is a dignified early-50s woman with an oval wheatish face, neat low bun, off-white sari with deep navy-gold border, charcoal coat, minimal gold jewellery, black shoes, and a dark-brown leather diplomatic folder with pen as her constant prop.

ramanuja.ref_desc: Ramanuja is a serene, medium-brown, clean-shaven South Indian acharya in late middle age with a small shikha, Sri Vaishnava tilaka, off-white dhoti in panchakacham style, cream and pale-yellow upper cloths with maroon and gold-ochre borders, tulasi beads, brown sandals, and he carries a long wooden palm-leaf manuscript bundle and a dark wooden staff.

basavanna_akka_mahadevi_and_allama_prabh.figure: Basavanna, Akka Mahadevi and Allama Prabhu
basavanna_akka_mahadevi_and_allama_prabh.ref_desc: Basavanna is a lean, mid-30s man with tied-back black hair, white upper cloth and saffron dhoti, rudraksha mala and ishtalinga, holding a palm-leaf roll; Akka Mahadevi is a slight young woman in an off-white sari and braid with ekatari; Allama Prabhu is a wiry older man in ochre tunic and brown lower cloth with damru, all in white, saffron and earthy browns.

dnyaneshwar.ref_desc: Dnyaneshwar is a serene late-teen Maharashtrian youth with shoulder-length black hair in a low knot, a sandal-tilak, off-white dhoti and upper cloth, pale saffron angavastra, tulsi mala, simple sandals, and a wrapped palm-leaf manuscript bundle with stylus.

chokhamela_and_soyarabai.ref_desc: Chokhamela, medium-brown, oval-faced, sparse-bearded man in off-white kurta, ochre dhoti, indigo shawl and pagadi with wooden staff, walks beside Soyarabai, medium-brown, round-faced woman in brick-red nauvari sari, olive choli and head-covered pallu holding a palm-leaf manuscript.

ravidas.ref_desc: Ravidas is a lean, medium-brown man in his late forties with a short beard, smooth back-tied dark hair under an off-white headcloth, wearing an off-white kurta, deep indigo dhoti, ochre shawl, simple sandals, and carrying a wooden cobbler’s board with leather and awl in earthy tones.

kabir.ref_desc: Kabir is a lean, medium-brown, grey-haired mystic in off-white kurta, cream dhoti, indigo vest, marigold angavastra and leather sandals, wearing a wooden bead mala and cotton skullcap, holding a brown handloom shuttle wrapped with indigo thread in a calm, intense pose.

mirabai.ref_desc: Mirabai is a slender wheatish-brown Rajput woman with large dark eyes, long black hair in a low bun under a saffron-orange odhani, wearing an off-white ghaghra, sky-blue choli, minimal gold jewellery, brown mojari shoes, and carrying a warm brown wooden tanpura.

nund_rishi.ref_desc: Nund Rishi is a slim Kashmiri saint with an oval light-brown face, short beard, wool cap, off-white wool pheran over ash-grey tunic, beige trousers, brown shoes, moss-green trim, and a simple wooden staff, in soft earthy tones.

muinuddin_chishti.ref_desc: An older Muinuddin Chishti with an oval wheatish face, short greying hair under a simple white turban, off-white kurta, taupe trousers, light brown wool cloak, muted indigo-edged shawl, brown sandals, and a plain wooden staff in a soft earthy palette.

baba_farid.ref_desc: Baba Farid appears as a late-60s Punjabi Sufi with an oval wheatish face, neat white beard, off-white turban, off-white cotton kurta, light brown wool shawl, beige trousers, dark brown sandals, and a dark wooden staff with a small cloth food pouch, in soft earth tones.

chaitanya_mahaprabhu.ref_desc: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu appears as a tall, slender wheatish‑complexioned man with shoulder‑length black hair, sandalwood tilaka, cream kurta, saffron dhoti with thin border, light‑yellow uttariya, tulasi necklace, bare feet, and brass kartal cymbals bound by red cord.

shah_abdul_latif_bhittai.ref_desc: Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai is a wheatish-complexioned, bearded Sindhi poet-saint in an ivory kurta, indigo waistcoat, sand-beige dhoti, maroon–indigo ajrak shawl, off-white turban, brown mojari shoes, carrying a wooden tanpura-like instrument with warm brown accents.

sala_and_vinayaditya.ref_desc: Vinayaditya Hoysaladeva is a sturdy, medium-brown warrior-king with black topknot, gold circlet, green tunic, maroon vest, cream dhoti, saffron sash, leather belt and sandals, simple gold jewellery, and a curved bronze-hilt sword at his left hip.

vishnuvardhana.ref_desc: Vishnuvardhana is a medium-brown, oval-faced Hoysala king with a gold band-crown, black hair knot, cream tunic, dark green silk shoulder drape, deep maroon bordered dhoti, gold jewellery, brown sandals, and a curved sword with red-wrapped wooden hilt at his left hip.

shantala_devi.ref_desc: Shantala Devi is a mid-20s, medium-brown, serene queen with long black hair in a low bun, maroon and gold South Indian silk sari, green blouse, gold jewellery, and a rolled palm-leaf manuscript, set in deep maroon, leaf green, warm gold and black tones.

veera_ballala_ii_and_umadevi.ref_desc: Veera Ballala II is a medium-brown, square-jawed king in a maroon tunic, cream trousers, dark-green angavastra, gold crown-band and sword, beside Umadevi, medium-brown, oval-faced queen in teal-blue sari, cream blouse, gold jewels and palm-leaf manuscript, both accented in gold and cream.

veera_ballala_iii.ref_desc: Veera Ballala III is a tall, broad-shouldered, medium-brown king with a warrior’s knot under a gold crown-band, maroon tunic, cream trousers, dark green dhoti drape, mustard-gold shawl, chainmail vest, gold armlets and a sheathed broad steel sword at his left hip.

hoysala_architects.ref_desc: Mid-30s Hoysala architect with medium-brown oval face, black knotted-bun hair and headband, wearing indigo tunic, cream dhoti, rust-orange shawl, brown sandals, gold chain, copper bangles, holding chisel and schist block in a deep indigo, cream and rust palette.

ruvari_mallitamma_dasoja_and_chavana.ref_desc: Ruvari Mallitamma is a late-30s Hoysala sculptor with medium-brown skin, black hair in a low knot and off-white headband, wearing an indigo tunic, cream dhoti, light-brown shoulder cloth, simple gold accents, and carrying an iron chisel and wooden mallet.

soma_dandanayaka.ref_desc: Soma Dandanayaka is a mid-30s Hoysala general with an oval medium-brown face, high-knot black hair and gold circlet, indigo padded tunic, sandstone-brown dhoti, marigold angavastra, bronze bracers, and a diagonally slung curved long sword in brown leather.

hoysala_tank_builders.ref_desc: A lean, medium-brown Hoysala tank builder with a short knot of black hair and headband, off-white tunic, cream dhoti, ochre shoulder shawl, simple sandals and jewellery, carrying a wooden measuring rod with rope and metal cup in an off-white, cream, ochre, dark-green, brown palette.

ketamalla_and_kesarasetti.ref_desc: Ketamalla and Kesarasetti are lean brown-complexioned Hoysala merchants with tied-back black hair, simple headbands, off-white dhotis, green and maroon upper cloths, cream angavastras, leather sandals, modest gold jewellery, a cloth coin-pouch and a rolled palm-leaf bundle in off-white, green, maroon and gold tones.

janna_harihara_and_raghavanka.ref_desc: Janna is a mid-30s slim Jain poet with an oval medium-brown face, short beard, black shoulder-length tied hair with an off-white headband, wearing off-white dhoti, cream angarakha, pale yellow shawl, dark maroon border and carrying a tied palm-leaf manuscript bundle.

kesiraja_and_rajaditya.ref_desc: Kesiraja and Rajaditya are two medium-brown Hoysala scholars: Kesiraja with off-white tunic, saffron dhoti, cream shawl and red-tied manuscript bundle; Rajaditya with blue-grey tunic, deep green dhoti, green sash and a wooden counting board, both with knotted black hair and sandals.

akka_mahadevi_basavanna_and_harihara.ref_desc: Akka Mahadevi, Basavanna and Harihara stand together with Akka in off-white sari and braid, Basavanna in pale tunic, indigo dhoti and red shawl, Harihara in cream kurta and green shawl, all holding a maroon-wrapped palm-leaf manuscript bundle.

rudradeva_of_anumakonda.ref_desc: Rudradeva appears as a lean medium-brown Deccan warrior-king with a high black topknot, indigo tunic, off-white dhoti, ochre sash, modest gold ornaments, brown sandals, and a plain iron-sheathed sword at his left hip in an indigo-maroon-ochre palette.

ganapati_deva.ref_desc: Ganapati Deva is a mid-40s, medium-brown Kakatiya king with shoulder-length tied black hair, a simple golden crown band, deep-red angavastra, beige upper garment, golden-ochre dhoti, light jewellery, and a curved sword in a brown scabbard, in deep red and ochre tones.

kakatiya_nayakas.ref_desc: Malyala Gunda Senani is a lean early-30s Kakatiya commander with medium-brown skin, black topknot, cream tunic, indigo vest, rust-red dhoti, mustard-yellow angavastra, light leather armour, and a curved steel sword at his left hip in a brown scabbard.

rudrama_devi.ref_desc: Rudrama Devi is a mid-30s, athletic, medium-brown queen with an oval strong-jawed face, long braided black hair under a gold coronet, red tunic, steel scale-mail vest, indigo dhoti, saffron sash, gold jewelry, and a curved steel talwar sword in a dark scabbard.

recherla_rudra.ref_desc: Recherla Rudra is a mid-30s, medium-brown, oval-faced warrior with a tight back-knot and maroon headband, wearing an off-white dhoti, cream angiya, maroon angavastra, dull-gold ornaments, leather sandals, and carrying a leaf-shaped sword in a brown scabbard.

prataparudra_ii.ref_desc: Prataparudra II is a mid-30s, medium-brown Kakatiya king with a warrior’s topknot, gold circlet, maroon quilted tunic, indigo shoulder cloth, cream trousers, steel chest-plate and armguards, disc-pommel sword at his hip, accented in golden yellow and steel grey.

ramappa_the_architect.ref_desc: Ramappa the Architect is a mid-40s lean man with an oval medium-brown face, low bun and dark headband, wearing off-white draped upper cloth over beige tunic and brown ankle-length dhoti with red sash, copper ornaments, and holding a palm-leaf manuscript roll and wooden measuring rod in warm earthy tones.

mailama_and_the_tank_builders.display_name: Mailama, Master of the Monsoon Tanks
mailama_and_the_tank_builders.ref_desc: Mailama is a lean, medium-brown Kakatiya engineer with a maroon turban, short beard, off-white angarakha, indigo waistcoat, mustard dhoti, diagonal sash and copper ornaments, carrying a marked wooden measuring staff in a palette of off-white, indigo and ochre.

rudradeva_and_kakatiya_stone_guilds.display_name: Rudradeva of the Kakatiya Stone Guilds
rudradeva_and_kakatiya_stone_guilds.ref_desc: Rudradeva appears as a lean, medium-brown Kakatiya king in maroon dhoti, cream tunic, off-white angavastra, gold circlet, modest jewellery, holding iron chisel and wooden mallet beside grey granite carving with maroon, off-white, gold-yellow, brown and grey tones.

jayapa_senani_and_tikkana.ref_desc: Jayapa Senani is a medium‑brown, sharp‑jawed Kakatiya officer with a small topknot, gold forehead band, maroon tunic under pale‑gold brigandine, green waist sash, cream trousers, brown bracers and sandals, carrying a sheathed Deccan sword and a palm‑leaf manuscript tube.

musunuri_kapaya_nayaka.ref_desc: Musunuri Kapaya Nayaka is a lean, medium-brown Deccan warrior with shoulder-length black hair in a low knot and maroon headband, wearing off-white tunic, indigo quilted jerkin, mustard sash, dark brown trousers, leather sandals, simple gold jewelry, and carrying a curved steel sword in a brown scabbard.

pushyamitra_shunga_and_menander_i.ref_desc: Pushyamitra is a broad-shouldered, wheatish man with a high black topknot and saffron headband, in off-white angarkha, mustard quilted coat, maroon belt, churidar trousers and brown boots with saffron shawl carrying a bamboo bow, beside Menander, a tall olive man with wavy brown hair, bronze diadem, off-white tunic, bronze cuirass, dark green cloak, leather boots and iron spear, all in a palette of saffron, maroon, off-white, mustard and dark green.

chandragupta_ii_vikramaditya_and_rudrasi.figure: Chandragupta II Vikramaditya and Rudrasimha III
chandragupta_ii_vikramaditya_and_rudrasi.ref_desc: Chandragupta II Vikramaditya has an oval, medium-brown face with a neat short beard, black hair in a high topknot under a simple gold circlet, wearing a deep maroon angarkha, off-white churidar, mustard-gold uttariya, brown boots and belt, and carrying a plain-hilted straight iron sword in a dark-brown scabbard.

yashodharman_and_mihirakula.ref_desc: Yashodharman has a medium-brown oval face, black topknot with a gold circlet, saffron tunic with olive quilted vest, cream angavastra and brown boots with a straight iron longsword, while Mihirakula has a lighter hawk-like face, rough shoulder-length dark hair with leather headband, steel-grey kaftan, dark leather lamellar cuirass, indigo trousers, charcoal cloak and a recurved composite bow with red-brown quiver.

harsha_vardhana_and_shashanka.ref_desc: Harsha Vardhana is a tall, athletic young man with a wheatish oval face, dark eyes, a small tilak, and dark hair in a high topknot with a slim gold circlet, wearing cream and maroon layered tunics over an off-white dhoti with a maroon belt, minimal gold jewellery, brown sandals, and carrying a simple long straight khadga in a brown leather scabbard; main colours are cream, maroon, gold, off-white and brown.

raja_dahir_and_muhammad_bin_qasim.figure: Raja Dahir and Muhammad bin Qasim
raja_dahir_and_muhammad_bin_qasim.ref_desc: Raja Dahir is a tall, wheatish-complexioned man in his early 40s with a topknot, tilak-marked forehead and gold circlet, wearing an off-white tunic, maroon sleeveless coat, saffron dhoti, indigo shawl and brown boots, carrying a simple curved steel sword at his left hip.

yashovarman_of_kannauj_and_lalitaditya_o.display_name: Yashovarman of Kannauj & Lalitaditya of Kashmir
yashovarman_of_kannauj_and_lalitaditya_o.figure: Yashovarman of Kannauj and Lalitaditya of Kashmir
yashovarman_of_kannauj_and_lalitaditya_o.ref_desc: Yashovarman is a medium-brown, oval-faced warrior-king with shoulder-length black hair in a low knot, deep red angarkha, quilted dull-gold vest, off-white dhoti, leather sandals and a plain curved sword, while Lalitaditya is a slightly lighter brown, broad-jawed king with wavy black hair in a high topknot, deep indigo wool tunic with saffron-cream borders, dark teal quilted vest, off-white close trousers, leather boots and a straight steel sword; both share a restrained gold-and-brown palette.

nagabhata_i_and_avanijanashraya_pulakesi.ref_desc: Nagabhata I has an oval wheatish-brown face with a short moustache and topknot bound by a golden headband, wearing a brick-red angarkha, indigo quilted vest, off-white leggings, brown boots, and belt-hung plain leather-scabbarded straight sword in muted reds, blues, and browns.

aditya_i_chola_and_aparajita_pallava.figure: Aditya I Chola and Aparajita Pallava
aditya_i_chola_and_aparajita_pallava.ref_desc: Athletic Aditya I with medium-brown oval face, black high topknot, deep-red angavastram over off-white tunic, golden-yellow veshti and sword at belt stands beside lean Aparajita with lower topknot, cream shawl, grey tunic, pale-blue veshti and round dark shield, in reds, yellows, creams, blues and browns.

krishna_iii_and_rajaditya_chola.ref_desc: Krishna III is a medium-brown, broad-shouldered man with a low bun, golden circlet, deep indigo quilted tunic, bronze breastplate, maroon sash and straight sword at his left hip, beside Rajaditya, a rich-brown, athletic man with a topknot, dark-red tunic, leather-and-bronze cuirass, off-white wrapped lower garment and a tall spear with a red cloth tie; both wear restrained gold jewellery in a palette of deep indigo, dark red, off-white, maroon and bronze.

tailapa_ii_and_karka_ii.ref_desc: Tailapa II is a lean, scar-cheeked Deccan king with a high black topknot, gold forehead band, indigo angarakha over cream sleeves, quilted brown vest, brick-red sash, ochre trousers, maroon shawl and a curved Deccan sword at his left hip, while Karka II is a dignified Rashtrakuta ruler with a lower black knot, modest conical crown, off-white dhoti with green border, mustard tunic, deep-green shawl, refined gold jewellery and a rolled palm-leaf charter bound with red cord.

jayapala_shahi_and_mahmud_of_ghazni.figure: Jayapala Shahi and Mahmud of Ghazni
jayapala_shahi_and_mahmud_of_ghazni.ref_desc: Jayapala is an older medium-brown North Indian king with greying shoulder-length hair under a deep-red cloth crown, wearing a muted teal quilted coat over off-white trousers and dark boots while holding a dark round shield with brass bosses, and Mahmud is a younger wheat-brown Ghaznavid commander with short dark hair under a steel helmet, dressed in a steel-grey scale coat over a dark indigo gambeson, tan trousers and dark riding boots, gripping a plain curved steel sword at his left side; both share a palette of muted teal, deep red, steel grey, dark indigo and tan.

suheldev_and_salar_masud.display_name: Suheldev of Bahraich & Ghazi Miyan (Salar Masud)
suheldev_and_salar_masud.ref_desc: A mid-20s Suheldev with wheatish oval face, low black warrior’s knot, forest-green quilted coat over off-white tunic and red trousers, brown belt and shoes, indigo sash and a simple curved sword beside a mid-20s Ghazi Miyan with light-brown face, white turban, sky-blue robe over off-white under-tunic, olive-green shawl, brown shoes and a long ash-wood spear, all in forest green, sky blue, off-white and brown tones.

jaichand_gahadavala_and_muhammad_of_ghor.figure: Jaichand Gahadavala and Muhammad of Ghor
jaichand_gahadavala_and_muhammad_of_ghor.ref_desc: Jaichand Gahadavala is a tall, athletic north Indian king with wheatish oval face, trimmed moustache-beard, red turban over tied-back black hair, wearing a deep maroon quilted coat over cream tunic, indigo trousers, muted gold shawl, minimal visible armour and brown boots, carrying a khanda sword at his left hip in a dark leather scabbard with brass fittings and dominated by maroon, cream, indigo, muted gold and brown colours.

raja_dahir_and_muhammad_ibn_qasim.figure: Raja Dahir and Muhammad ibn Qasim
raja_dahir_and_muhammad_ibn_qasim.ref_desc: Raja Dahir is a sturdy late-40s Sindhi king with medium-brown skin, long black hair tied under a golden turban, saffron angarkha, olive quilted vest and maroon sash carrying a curved sword, beside young Muhammad ibn Qasim in beige tunic, brown lamellar armour, dark-green cloak and straight sword.

nagabhata_i_and_avanijanashraya_pulakesh.ref_desc: Nagabhata I is a mid-30s dusky warrior with an oval face, short beard, black hair tied in a low knot with a red band, wearing a saffron angarkha, off-white trousers, quilted dark-brown vest, red sash, ankle boots, bronze circlet, and a plain leather-sheathed iron sword at his waist in muted saffron, dark red, off-white, dark brown and bronze tones.

prithviraj_chauhan_iii_and_muhammad_of_g.display_name: Prithviraj of Ajmer & Muhammad of Ghor
prithviraj_chauhan_iii_and_muhammad_of_g.figure: Prithviraj Chauhan III and Muhammad of Ghor
prithviraj_chauhan_iii_and_muhammad_of_g.ref_desc: Prithviraj is a wheatish-complexioned Rajput in deep-maroon quilted armour over cream tunic and mustard churidar with red-and-gold turban, green sash, bow and quiver, beside Muhammad of Ghor, a light-olive commander in dark-indigo tunic, mail hauberk, conical helmet and curved sword, all in maroon, yellow, indigo, olive and steel tones.

jayachandra_of_the_gahadavala_dynasty.ref_desc: Jayachandra of Kannauj is a mid-40s, tall, medium-brown North Indian king with an oval face, neat moustache-beard, dark eyes, a low maroon turban over tied-back hair, wearing a deep indigo quilted coat over cream garments with mail and steel plate, crimson waist-sash, brown leather boots, minimal gold jewellery, and carrying a straight steel khanda in a brown scabbard.

alauddin_khalji_and_ratnasimha.ref_desc: Alauddin Khalji and Ratnasimha stand side by side, Alauddin in dark green quilted coat over mail and lamellar, war-turbaned helmet and shamshir, Ratnasimha in saffron-ochre angarkha over mail and breastplate, Rajput turban, talwar and shield, in green, saffron, maroon, cream and steel grey tones.

prataparudra_ii_and_ulugh_khan.ref_desc: Prataparudra is a sturdy medium-brown Telugu king with a black topknot, maroon silk angarakha, off-white dhoti, green gold-bordered sashes and a sheathed curved sword, while Ulugh Khan is tall, indigo-quilted, turban-helmed with mail hints, off-white trousers, brown boots and a straight sword.

qutb_al_din_aibak_and_sulakshanapala.ref_desc: Qutb al-Din Aibak is a tall, broad-shouldered man in his early 40s with a trimmed black beard, short hair under a dark indigo conical cap, wearing an indigo quilted coat with mail over beige tunic and trousers, brown boots, dark indigo cloak, and a plain curved shamshir at his left hip in a brown scabbard, all in deep indigo, muted red, beige, brown leather and dull steel grey tones.

sitaladeva_songara_and_alauddin_khalji.ref_desc: Sitaladeva Songara has a wheatish oval face with a trimmed mustache-beard, black hair in a low knot under a deep-red Marwari turban, saffron quilted tunic over mail with off-white churidar and brown boots, wielding a brass-hilted talwar, beside Alauddin Khalji in emerald-green quilted coat, steel helmet, dark trousers, black boots and mail, holding a rolled parchment map; their colours are saffron, deep red, emerald green, dark blue and steel grey.

francisco_de_almeida_and_amir_hussain_al.display_name: Francisco de Almeida & Amir Hussain Al-Kurdi
francisco_de_almeida_and_amir_hussain_al.figure: Francisco de Almeida and Amir Hussain Al-Kurdi
francisco_de_almeida_and_amir_hussain_al.ref_desc: Francisco de Almeida is a broad-shouldered, tanned, square-faced Iberian with short greying hair under a dark crimson beret, green quilted doublet, brown leather jerkin, cream shirt, brown hose and boots, brass-hilted sword, while Amir Hussain Al-Kurdi is a lean, light-brown, oval-faced bearded admiral in a white turban with green band, indigo naval coat, dark green reinforced vest, sand trousers, brown shoes and a slender sabre at his hip, their shared palette of dark green, indigo, brown, cream and dark red unifying the design.

rana_kumbha_and_mahmud_khalji_of_malwa.figure: Rana Kumbha and Mahmud Khalji of Malwa
rana_kumbha_and_mahmud_khalji_of_malwa.ref_desc: Rana Kumbha has a long-jawed face, wheatish complexion, black hair in a low knot under a red turban with white plume, maroon quilted angarkha over mail, mustard sash, off-white churidar and boots with sword and round shield, while Mahmud Khalji has a medium-brown face with trimmed beard, dark green conical turban, dark green quilted coat and lamellar over mail, cream trousers, cloak, curved saber and buckler, all in deep maroon, mustard yellow, dark green, cream and steel grey tones.

mahmud_begada_and_patai_rawal.ref_desc: Mahmud Begada is a wheatish, broad-faced young sultan with a dark-green conical turban, quilted dark-green jama over cream garments, leather boots and a sheathed talwar, facing Patai Rawal, a sun-browned Rajput with shoulder-length hair, saffron headband, off-white angarkha, rust-red battlevest and his own talwar, all in dark green, cream, deep red, rust red and brown tones.

rana_sanga_and_mahmud_khalji_ii.figure: Rana Sanga and Mahmud Khalji II
rana_sanga_and_mahmud_khalji_ii.ref_desc: Rana Sanga is a tall, broad-shouldered Rajput in a bottle-green mail coat over an off-white quilted angarkha, saffron-orange waist sash, white churidar trousers, brown riding boots, red pagri with white feather, facial scar, and a plain-hilted talwar at his left hip.

rani_durgavati_and_asaf_khan.ref_desc: Rani Durgavati is a medium-brown, sharp-eyed woman in her early 30s with a long black braid, deep-red padded blouse, marigold angarkha coat, dark green ghagra, indigo dupatta, brown leather belt, modest gold jewellery, and a brass-hilted talwar at her left hip.

sher_shah_suri_and_rao_maldev_rathore.display_name: Sher Shah Suri & Rao Maldev Rathore
sher_shah_suri_and_rao_maldev_rathore.figure: Sher Shah Suri and Rao Maldev Rathore
sher_shah_suri_and_rao_maldev_rathore.ref_desc: Sher Shah Suri is a sturdy, wheat-brown, square-faced man with a neat dark-grey beard, short hair under a dark-green Afghan turban-helmet, wearing a quilted dark-green qaba, cream tunic, brown churidar and steel breastplate with brown boots and plain talwar, while Rao Maldev Rathore is a tall, sun-browned Rajput with an oval face, black hair in a knot under a saffron-orange pagri, indigo blue angarkha with subtle patterns, off-white churidar, maroon waist sash, simple steel breastplate, brown jutti shoes and a brass-hilted Rajput talwar in a red scabbard.

babur_and_rana_sanga.ref_desc: Babur is a lean, mid-30s Timurid in a deep red-brown quilted coat with teal under-tunic, dark teal cap and a curved sabre, while Rana Sanga is a tall Rajput in indigo angarkha, mail-and-plate armour, cream dhoti, saffron scarf, steel helmet and straight khanda, all in deep red-brown, teal, cream, indigo and saffron tones.

babur_and_mahmud_lodi.display_name: Zahir-ud-din Muhammad Babur vs. Mahmud Lodi
babur_and_mahmud_lodi.ref_desc: Babur is a lean, fair-olive man in a muted warm-red quilted jama, deep-green turban cap, dark-teal under-tunic, cream churidar and brown boots with a plain tulwar, facing Mahmud Lodi, a medium-brown, broad-shouldered Afghan in indigo tunic, brown leather-plated coat, white Afghan turban and off-white trousers with an Afghan sword, all in earthy reds, greens, indigo and browns.

sher_shah_suri_and_humayun.ref_desc: Humayun is a late-30s tall, lean Mughal emperor with light brown complexion, trimmed moustache and pointed beard, wearing a dark emerald green turban with a white feather, a deep teal quilted jamma over cream tunic and off-white paijama, maroon patka, dark brown riding boots, and a dark red-sheathed talwar at his left hip accented by gold details.

hemu_bairam_khan_and_akbar.display_name: Hemu, Bairam Khan & Akbar – Second Battle of Panipat
hemu_bairam_khan_and_akbar.ref_desc: Hemu is a sturdy middle-aged commander in mustard-yellow breastplate, maroon turban and off-white quilted armour with a talwar; young Akbar is lean in cream quilted jama, light-bronze cuirass and green turban; Bairam Khan is tall in dark-blue velvet jama, mail cuirass and blue-sheathed talwar.

maharana_pratap_and_man_singh_i.display_name: Maharana Pratap & Man Singh at Haldighati
maharana_pratap_and_man_singh_i.figure: Maharana Pratap and Man Singh I
maharana_pratap_and_man_singh_i.ref_desc: Maharana Pratap has a wheatish-tan face with a scar, thick moustache, mustard-yellow turban with red band and green plume, off-white quilted angarkha, steel mail and bronze breastplate, emerald trousers, crimson kamarband, brown boots, Rajput sword and steel shield, while Man Singh has a fairer face with curved moustache, deep-red turban with gold sarpech and teal feather, yellow-gold silk jama over mail, steel breastplate, azure trousers, dark-red kamarband, tan boots and an ornate talwar with polished shield, all in mustard yellow, deep red, emerald green, steel grey and yellow-gold tones.

thomas_best_and_jahangir.ref_desc: Thomas Best has a sunburned square face, wavy brown hair under a black hat, navy doublet and olive breeches with a leather jerkin and cutlass, beside Jahangir with light-brown oval face, pale-gold striped turban, cream floral jama, green sash, jade-handled fly-whisk and shamshir in green scabbard, all in navy, brown, cream, pale gold and deep green tones.

jai_singh_i_and_shivaji.display_name: Jai Singh I & Shivaji at Purandar, 1665
jai_singh_i_and_shivaji.ref_desc: Jai Singh I is an older broad-built Rajput in an off-white angarkha, maroon quilted coat, mustard churidar, saffron shawl, orange turban and talwar, facing a lean mid-30s Shivaji in a white gold-edged jama, rust-orange churidar, saffron patka, white turban, Maratha sword and rolled parchment, all in warm saffron, maroon and off-white tones.

aurangzeb_and_sikandar_adil_shah.ref_desc: Aurangzeb is a lean, grey-bearded older man with a long face and calm austere expression, wearing a tall white turban with a green plume, an ivory-and-gold striped jama, maroon sash, moss-green churidar, beige quilted vest, brown mojari shoes, and holding a rolled cream farman with red ribbon.

aurangzeb_and_abul_hasan_qutb_shah.figure: Aurangzeb and Abul Hasan Qutb Shah
aurangzeb_and_abul_hasan_qutb_shah.ref_desc: Aurangzeb is a wiry, older Mughal emperor with a long narrow face, grey pointed beard, tall white muslin turban, ivory striped jama with quilted light-cream sleeveless coat, olive-green sash and churidar, brown leather khussa shoes, and a plain brown-sheathed talwar on an olive-green baldric.

bahadur_shah_i_and_azam_shah.figure: Bahadur Shah I and Azam Shah
bahadur_shah_i_and_azam_shah.ref_desc: Bahadur Shah I has an oval wheatish face with a trimmed black-and-grey beard, emerald turban, cream-and-gold jama, green sash and sheathed talwar, while Azam Shah has an angular wheatish-olive face with fuller beard, crimson turban, pale-blue jama, red sash and drawn talwar, all in Mughal battlefield attire.

nadir_shah_and_muhammad_shah.ref_desc: Nadir Shah is a wiry, tanned, scar-cheeked man in deep-indigo quilted coat, mail hauberk, sand trousers, brown boots, red-banded steel helmet and dark-blue cloak wielding a simple shamshir, beside Muhammad Shah, a wheat-complexioned ruler in emerald-green gold-patterned jama, maroon sash, cream shawl, pale-gold striped jewelled turban and red mojari holding a sheathed green-scabbarded talwar.

akbar_jaimal_and_patta.ref_desc: Young Akbar with emerald green gold‑patterned jama, cream churidar, maroon sash, green‑striped turban and jade‑hilt talwar stands opposite stern armoured Jaimal in saffron turban and spear, and spirited armoured Patta in sky‑blue turban with sun‑motif shield, all in deep green, maroon, saffron, sky blue and steel grey tones.

anandapala.ref_desc: Anandapala is a tall, early-40s North Indian king with a medium-tan oval face, mustache and short beard, long black hair in a knot under a deep-red turban, indigo quilted war-vest over an off-white tunic, olive trousers, brown boots, ochre shawl, and a plain-hilt curved steel sword at his left hip.

bhima_i_and_the_somnath_defenders.display_name: Bhima I and the Somnath Defenders
bhima_i_and_the_somnath_defenders.figure: Bhima I and the Somnath defenders
bhima_i_and_the_somnath_defenders.ref_desc: Bhima I is a tall, broad-shouldered man in his early 30s with a wheatish oval face, black hair in a topknot under a dark-red gold-trimmed turban, wearing a cream angarakha, maroon quilted war-vest, off-white trousers, indigo kamarband, brown sandals, modest gold jewellery, and a plain curved sword in a brown leather scabbard.

trilochanapala.ref_desc: Trilochanapala is a late‑30s, lean, wheat‑brown, oval‑faced Hindu Shahi king with a neat beard, scar on his left cheek, dark brown hair in a high topknot with a red headband and simple gold circlet, wearing an off‑white tunic under a dark indigo quilted jacket, brown churidar trousers, brick red shawl, brown leather boots and bracers, and carrying a plain slightly curved Indian sword in a dark brown scabbard.

raisal_and_bhikan.ref_desc: Raisal and Bhikan Khokhar are shown as a single lean, wheatish warrior with an oval face, low deep-red turban over a black hair knot, trimmed beard, indigo quilted kurta, forest-green shawl, brown leather vest and boots, and a curved steel sword in a brown scabbard.

paramardi_and_trailokyavarman.ref_desc: Paramardi and Trailokyavarman are two Chandela princes: Paramardi older with a saffron-ochre quilted war-kurta, off-white dhoti, red shawl, low knot and small plume, straight sword at his hip; Trailokyavarman younger in indigo quilted coat, higher knot, red shawl-cloak and curved sword.

zafar_khan.ref_desc: Zafar Khan is a tall, athletic, warm-brown-complexioned Delhi general with an oval face, cheek scar, moustache and short beard, dark hair in a warrior’s knot under a steel conical helmet with red turban-wrap, wearing indigo quilted coat, steel mail, off-white tunic, dark-olive trousers, brown boots, crimson sash, leather bracers and belt, and wielding a plain steel talwar in a brown scabbard with an indigo, crimson, olive, steel, and brown palette.

ghazi_malik.ref_desc: Ghazi Malik is a mid-30s tall, broad-shouldered frontier commander with wheat-brown skin, sharp dark eyes, a trimmed mustache and short pointed beard, straight black hair under a conical steel helmet, wearing an off-white tunic, brown trousers, deep indigo quilted gambeson beneath a dull-steel mail-and-plate coat, dark-olive cloak, brown leather boots and belt, and carrying a slightly curved Indo-Turkic sword in a brown scabbard at his left hip.

hammira.ref_desc: Hammira of Ranthambhore is a mid-30s, broad-shouldered Rajput king with a wheatish complexion, trimmed beard, scarred left cheek, black hair in a low knot under a crimson turban, wearing an indigo quilted qaba over mail with cream churidar, saffron sash and leather boots, carrying a brass-hilted talwar in a brown scabbard in a deep indigo, crimson, saffron and cream palette.

rao_daljit_and_mahmud_tughlaq.ref_desc: Rao Daljit has a wheatish oval face with moustache and short beard, black hair in a knot under a deep-red pagri, wearing a marigold quilted coat over mail, off-white churidar and brown boots with a brass-hilt talwar, while Mahmud Tughlaq has a medium-brown oval face, short beard, indigo cloth-wrapped conical helm, dark indigo tunic under steel lamellar, grey trousers, black boots and an olive belt, both in marigold yellow, deep red, indigo blue, steel grey and olive green tones.

jassa_singh_ahluwalia.ref_desc: Jassa Singh Ahluwalia is a mid-40s broad-shouldered Sikh leader with wheatish complexion, short black-and-grey beard, navy-blue domed dastar, deep navy chola over indigo garments, mustard-ochre kamarband, brown leather belts and jutti, and a plain steel-hilted talwar in a brown scabbard.

muhammad_shah_and_delhi_s_residents.ref_desc: Muhammad Shah is a late-30s Mughal emperor with a light brown oval face, short beard, cream turban with emerald sarpech, wearing a rose-red patterned silk jama, green quilted sleeveless coat, off-white churidar, brown mojari shoes, and a sheathed dark-brown-scurabbarded talwar at his hip in rose red, bottle green, cream, pale gold and off-white tones.

bhima_i_and_kumarapala.display_name: Bhima I & Kumarapala of Chaulukya Gujarat
bhima_i_and_kumarapala.ref_desc: Bhima I and Kumarapala stand together, both medium-brown Gujarati kings with black topknots, Bhima in off-white angarkha, deep-red dhoti and indigo shawl holding a palm-leaf manuscript and wooden measuring rod, Kumarapala in cream angarkha, pale-green dhoti, maroon shawl, small gold crown and copper kalasha, all in warm off-white, red, indigo, cream and maroon tones.

al_biruni_and_chand_bardai.ref_desc: Depict al-Biruni as a late-40s Khurasani scholar with light wheat complexion, white cap with teal band, off-white robe, teal coat, brown belt and book with astrolabe, alongside Chand Bardai, a late-30s Rajput bard with warm brown skin, tied shoulder-length hair, cream angarkha, indigo dhoti, maroon sash, sandals and a small lute with manuscript, in a teal, maroon, indigo and brown palette.

muhammad_bin_bakhtiyar_khalji.ref_desc: Muhammad bin Bakhtiyar Khalji is a lean, medium-tan cavalry commander with a sharp oval face, shoulder-length black hair under a dark quilted war cap, wearing an off‑white tunic, steel-grey quilted coat, dark trousers, brown riding boots, deep-red sash and cloak, and carrying a plain curved sabre in a brown leather scabbard, dominated by steel grey, deep red, brown leather, off‑white and dark brown tones.

alauddin_khalji_and_ramachandra_yadava.ref_desc: Alauddin Khalji is a lean, late-20s warrior with a wheatish oval face, black hair under a dark green quilted war-turban, forest-green quilted qaba over mail, off-white churidar and brown boots, wielding a plain steel talwar with red sash accents, while Ramachandra Yadava is a sturdier, late-40s king with a medium-brown broad face, wavy shoulder-length dark hair under a simple golden turban, wearing a muted saffron angarkha with red borders over a white dhoti and green sash, holding a carved wooden staff with a metal cap; both are fully and modestly clothed in era-accurate garments using forest green, deep red, muted saffron, white and brown leather tones.

babur_and_medini_rai.ref_desc: Medini Rai is a late-30s Rajput chief with a wheatish angular face, short beard, maroon-and-mustard turban, off-white quilted gambeson under mail, deep indigo sleeveless surcoat, mustard trousers, brown boots, maroon sash and belt, carrying a curved talwar at his left hip.

munim_khan_and_daud_khan_karrani.display_name: Munim Khan vs Daud Khan Karrani
munim_khan_and_daud_khan_karrani.figure: Munim Khan and Daud Khan Karrani
munim_khan_and_daud_khan_karrani.ref_desc: Munim Khan is a late-middle-aged, medium-tan Mughal general with a red turban, maroon striped jama, olive quilted sleeveless coat, cream churidar, brown boots, and a gold-hilted talwar, facing Daud Khan, a younger, wheatish Afghan in a dark green turban, teal tunic, brown lamellar leather vest, off-white trousers, brown boots, and wielding a long straight spear; both share a palette of maroon, dark teal, cream, olive, and dark green.

banda_singh_bahadur_and_wazir_khan.display_name: Banda Singh Bahadur vs Wazir Khan
banda_singh_bahadur_and_wazir_khan.figure: Banda Singh Bahadur and Wazir Khan
banda_singh_bahadur_and_wazir_khan.ref_desc: Banda Singh Bahadur is a lean mid-30s Sikh warrior with an orange turban, long black beard, deep-indigo chola, saffron sash, steel breastplate and khanda sword, while Wazir Khan is a dignified older Mughal in an indigo turban, emerald-gold jama, mail coat and curved talwar, all in indigo, saffron, emerald, maroon and steel tones.

robert_clive_and_siraj_ud_daulah.ref_desc: Siraj ud-Daulah is a late-teen slim Nawab with a wheatish complexion, oval face, short dark hair under an emerald green Mughal turban, wearing a deep red gold-patterned angarkha, cream churidar, green patka, cream shawl, gold jewellery, brown mojari shoes, and carrying a brass-hilted talwar in a brown scabbard.

louis_paradis_and_mahfuz_khan.ref_desc: Louis Paradis is a compact late-30s French officer with a sun-browned oval face, dark queue, black tricorn, navy coat with red facings, buff breeches and a brass-hilt smallsword, beside Mahfuz Khan, a tall brown-complexioned prince in a white turban, green angarkha, grey quilted vest, cream churidar and talwar in a dark red scabbard, all in navy, deep green, golden yellow, cream and dark red tones.

eyre_coote_and_comte_de_lally.figure: Eyre Coote and Comte de Lally
eyre_coote_and_comte_de_lally.ref_desc: Coote is a lean fair British officer with light brown queued hair, black gold-trimmed tricorn, scarlet coat with navy facings, white waistcoat, buff breeches and a brass-hilt small-sword, while Lally is a broad French officer with powdered hair, navy coat with red facings, cream waistcoat, beige breeches and a brass-guard sabre; both wear black buckle shoes and share a palette of scarlet, deep navy, white, buff and black.

hector_munro_and_shah_alam_ii.display_name: Hector Munro & Shah Alam II (Dual Character Sheet)
hector_munro_and_shah_alam_ii.figure: Hector Munro and Shah Alam II
hector_munro_and_shah_alam_ii.ref_desc: Hector Munro is a fair, sharp‑featured officer in a scarlet British uniform with white breeches, black bicorne hat, and brass‑hilted sabre, standing beside Shah Alam II, a light‑brown Mughal emperor in cream‑and‑gold jama, green sash, pearl necklace, and turban, holding a rolled cream farman scroll; their shared palette is scarlet, cream, gold, dark green, and black.

parshuram_bhau_patwardhan_and_nizam_ali_.figure: Parshuram Bhau Patwardhan and Nizam Ali Khan
parshuram_bhau_patwardhan_and_nizam_ali_.ref_desc: Parshuram Bhau Patwardhan is a lean early-forties Maratha commander with a deep-saffron turban, short black hair, neat upturned moustache and cheek scar, wearing a white quilted angarkha, dark-brown studded leather jerkin, saffron sash, white churidars, brown boots and carrying a curved talwar at his left hip.

tipu_sultan_and_george_harris.ref_desc: Tipu Sultan and George Harris stand side by side: Tipu in a cream-and-dark-green striped jama, dark-green turban and war coat with brown shoes, gripping a curved Mysorean sabre, and Harris in a red and navy gold-trimmed British general’s coat with bicorne hat and straight smallsword, using a dark green, off-white, red, navy and gold palette.

arthur_wellesley_and_daulat_rao_scindia.figure: Arthur Wellesley and Daulat Rao Scindia
arthur_wellesley_and_daulat_rao_scindia.ref_desc: Tall, lean Arthur Wellesley with fair weathered face, short wavy dark brown hair and a navy bicorne, wearing a navy tailcoat with red facings, buff breeches, black riding boots, white crossbelt and buff waist belt, carrying a plain brass-hilted officer’s sword.

sham_singh_attariwala_and_hugh_gough.figure: Sham Singh Attariwala and Hugh Gough
sham_singh_attariwala_and_hugh_gough.ref_desc: Sham Singh Attariwala is an older, lean Punjabi Sikh with a white beard tied close, a deep navy-blue turban with a small steel chakram, wearing a deep navy angarkha, steel-grey quilted coat, mustard-yellow sash, white salwar, brown boots, and carrying a brass-hilted talwar sword in a brown scabbard.

gopala_i.ref_desc: Gopala I is a medium-brown, strong-jawed man in his late 30s with a neat moustache and short beard, black hair in a high topknot under a simple gold circlet, wearing a deep indigo tunic, off-white dhoti, ochre uttariya, brown leather belt and bracers, gold jewellery, and carrying a plain-hilted straight sword in a brown scabbard at his left hip.

dharmapala.ref_desc: Dharmapala is a wheat-brown, oval-faced man in his 40s with a black topknot, neat moustache and beard, wearing a maroon upper wrap, cream ankle-length dhoti with gold borders, saffron shawl, simple gold jewellery, and carrying a curved steel sword in a dark brown scabbard with gold fittings.

devapala_and_balaputradeva.ref_desc: Devapala is a medium-brown, oval-faced, bearded man in a cream long-sleeved coat, red dhoti, red-gold sashes, simple coronet and sword, while Balaputradeva is warm-brown, clean-shaven, long-haired in a topknot, in light-blue tunic, indigo sarong, gold-yellow sash and carrying a rolled palm-leaf manuscript.

mahipala_i.ref_desc: Mahipala I is a tall, broad-shouldered Bengali king with medium-brown skin, neat moustache and short beard, black hair in a low knot under a dark-red cloth turban, wearing an off-white angarkha, deep-green embroidered shawl, maroon dhoti, gold belt and jewellery, brown sandals, and a curved steel sword in a dark-brown scabbard at his left hip.

vijayasena.ref_desc: Vijayasena is a medium-brown, sharp-eyed, mustached man in his early 40s with a black warrior topknot and maroon headband, wearing a deep indigo quilted armour vest over a cream tunic, off-white bordered dhoti, brick-red silk uttariya, simple gold jewellery, brown sandals and carrying a curved single-edged sword in a dark-brown scabbard.

divya_and_ramapala.ref_desc: Divya is a lean, wheat‑brown north‑Bengal warrior with a short beard, medium black hair in a small topknot, off‑white torso wrap, deep‑green sleeveless coat, brick‑red dhoti and bamboo spear, while Ramapala is a taller, dignified king with fuller beard, high topknot under a maroon headwrap with gold band, golden‑yellow silk drape over indigo tunic, maroon gold‑bordered dhoti and curved sword at his hip, both in off‑white, deep green, brick red, indigo and golden yellow tones.

lakshmanasena_vishvarupasena_and_keshava.ref_desc: Three related Bengali Sena rulers share similar angular faces and topknotted hair: Lakshmanasena in maroon silk over cream tunic and off-white dhoti, Vishvarupasena in indigo tunic with quilted brown vest and ochre dhoti, and Keshavasena in pale-green long tunic with cream dhoti, all accompanied by a single shared dark-sheathed pata sword and a palette of maroon, indigo, cream, muted gold and pale green.

dharmapala_and_atisha.display_name: Dharmapala & Atiśa of the Pāla Mahāvihāras
dharmapala_and_atisha.ref_desc: Dharmapala is a lean, medium-brown Pāla emperor with a black topknot, gold circlet, deep-red cloak over cream tunic and mustard-ochre dhoti, sword at his hip, beside the shaven-headed Atiśa in plain saffron patchwork robes holding tied palm-leaf manuscripts, in a red, ochre, cream and gold palette.

bengal_merchants_and_grant_scribes.ref_desc: A medium-brown, oval-faced early-30s Bengali man with straight black hair in a low knot and white headband, wearing an off-white dhoti and uttariya with deep-red borders, simple gold hoops, leather belt and sandals, holding a copper-plate grant with seal and reed pen beside a bowl of cowries.

pala_metalworkers_and_monks.ref_desc: A slim, medium-brown Pala-era artisan-monk with an oval face, black hair in a short topknot with a saffron headband, wearing saffron dhoti, maroon shawl, off-white tunic, leather belt and sandals, holding a bronze Bodhisattva statue and chisel in bronze-gold, maroon and saffron tones.

ballalasena.ref_desc: Ballalasena is a medium-tall, late-middle-aged king with a medium-brown oval face, black hair in a high Brahmin topknot, cream angavastra and off-white dhoti with mustard-gold borders, deep maroon uttariya, simple gold jewellery, and a palm-leaf manuscript bundle tied with a red cord.

jayadeva.ref_desc: Jayadeva is a slender, mid-30s poet with medium-brown oval face, black hair in a low knot with a cream headband, wearing off-white shawl, cream upper wrap, turmeric-yellow Bengali dhoti, simple beads and bangles, and holding a palm-leaf manuscript bundle with stylus in maroon-cream tones.

pala_scribes_and_tibetan_monks.ref_desc: Vidyakar is a medium-brown, sharp-gazed Pala scribe with shoulder-length tied-back black hair, cream uttariya and deep indigo dhoti, beside Tenzin, a fair coppery Tibetan monk with shaved stubble, maroon chuba, saffron shirt, dark trousers and boots, jointly carrying a wrapped palm-leaf manuscript bundle with wooden covers in cream, indigo, maroon, saffron and dark-brown tones.

durlabhavardhana.ref_desc: Durlabhavardhana is a late-30s Kashmiri king with an oval wheat-toned face, dark hair in a high knot under a maroon conical cap, deep green tunic, cream trousers, saffron shawl, gold naga jewellery, a sword at his hip, and a gold dinar in hand.

candrapida.ref_desc: Candrapida (Vajraditya) has an oval wheatish face, short beard, black hair in a topknot with gold circlet, deep indigo royal tunic, cream trousers, muted crimson cloak, brown boots, gold accents, and a curved steel sword with red-wrapped hilt and turquoise pommel.

lalitaditya_muktapida.ref_desc: Lalitaditya Muktapida is a mid-30s Kashmiri king with shoulder-length dark hair in a low knot, saffron tunic, cream wool shawl, off-white dhoti, modest gold circlet and jewellery, carrying a sheathed straight steel sword, in saffron, deep red, cream, muted green, and brown tones.

the_martand_sun_temple.ref_desc: The Spirit of Martand Sun Temple is a tall, athletic Kashmiri man with amber-brown eyes, shoulder-length black hair in a low knot with a pale saffron headband, wearing a stone-grey choga over off-white tunic and trousers, a sky-blue trefoil-edged shawl and brown boots, carrying a pale grey limestone model of Martand’s trefoil-arched gateway.

parihasapura_patrons.ref_desc: Parihasapura Patron is a lean, bearded Kashmiri man with dark brown hair and gold headband, in saffron tunic, cream trousers, indigo shawl, maroon belt, gold pendant, holding a red‑tied palm‑leaf manuscript bundle, using saffron, indigo, cream, maroon and gold colors.

durlabhavardhana_and_lalitaditya.ref_desc: Durlabhavardhana has a rounded wheatish face, low‑knot dark hair, white angarkha, saffron shawl, red trousers, scroll in hand, while Lalitaditya has a longer face, high‑knot hair, cream quilted tunic, bronze scale armour, blue cloak, sword, with white, saffron, red, blue, and bronze tones.

atrigupta_and_saktisvamin.ref_desc: Atrigupta and Śaktisvāmin are two modestly robed Brahmin scholars with sandalwood tilaka and high black topknots in off-white and pale-yellow dhotis, cream and white shawls, wooden wrist malas and sandals, sharing a maroon-edged palm-leaf manuscript bundle in warm muted tones.

the_nilamata_purana.ref_desc: A mid-40s Kashmiri sage with an oval light-brown face, dark brown hair in a low knot with off-white headband, wearing a saffron choga, cream tunic, off-white dhoti, slate-grey indigo-bordered shawl and brown sandals, holding a palm-leaf manuscript in saffron, cream, grey, indigo and brown tones.

jayapida_vinayaditya.ref_desc: Jayapida Vinayaditya is a tall, athletic Kashmiri king with an oval wheatish face, black topknot hair under a golden diadem, deep blue tunic, cream shawl and trousers, brown boots, simple gold ornaments, and a plain long steel sword with bronze-fitted scabbard in a blue-cream-red-brown-green palette.

cippatajayapida_and_jayadevi_s_brothers.ref_desc: Mid-30s Kashmiri regent with oval wheatish face, low-knot dark hair and gold circlet, in deep indigo tunic, pale saffron shawl, off-white trousers, dark red sash, dark brown boots, carrying a mixed coin-pouch and palm-leaf seal in a gold-accented palette.

kalhana.ref_desc: Kalhaṇa is a mid-30s Kashmiri poet with an oval wheatish face, low-knotted black hair under a dark brown cap, saffron tunic, forest-green shawl, off-white trousers, brown shoes, and always carries a rolled palm-leaf manuscript with a bronze stylus, in warm saffron and green tones.

anantavarman_chodaganga_deva.ref_desc: Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva is a tall, medium-brown Eastern Ganga emperor with an oval face, high black hair knot bound by a gold band, maroon silk dhoti, golden-yellow sash-angavastra, cream uttariya, simple gold jewellery, and a plain curved steel sword in a brown scabbard, using maroon, gold, cream and dark green tones.

anangabhima_deva_iii.ref_desc: Anangabhima Deva III is a tall, medium-brown Ganga king with a neat moustache and jawline beard, black hair in a high topknot and gold circlet, wearing cream dhoti, pale-gold angarakha, maroon silk uttariya, gold Jagannath necklace, leather sandals, and carrying a plain curved sword at his left hip in a wooden scabbard, all in a cream, maroon, pale gold, dark brown, and black palette.

narasimhadeva_i.ref_desc: Narasimhadeva I has an oval wheatish face with a neat moustache and beard, black hair in a high topknot with a gold crest, wearing a crimson dhoti, golden-yellow tunic, cream striped uttariya, gold jewellery, sandals, and a curved Kalinga sword at his left hip with these colours dominant.

chandrika_devi.ref_desc: Chandrika Devi is a late-20s Odia royal woman with medium-brown skin, black hair in a low bun with gold band and jasmine, in a deep maroon sari with mustard-gold borders, teal choli, gold jewellery, brown slippers, and holding a red-tied palm-leaf manuscript.

anangabhima_deva_iii_and_general_vishnu.figure: Anangabhima Deva III and general Vishnu
anangabhima_deva_iii_and_general_vishnu.ref_desc: Anangabhima Deva III and General Vishnu appear as two medium-brown, strong-built men with topknot hairstyles, saffron and indigo dhoti-based war garb, modest bronze armour, a Jagannath-themed sword and a leather-wrapped spear, in a palette of saffron, green, indigo, bronze, and dark brown.

narasimhadeva_i_and_tughril_tughan_khan.figure: Narasimhadeva I and Tughril Tughan Khan
narasimhadeva_i_and_tughril_tughan_khan.ref_desc: Narasimhadeva I is a mid-30s, athletic Odishan king with medium-brown complexion, black hair tied in a short knot under a gold lotus headband, wearing deep-red angavastra, saffron dhoti, ivory tunic, leather belt and boots, gold armlet, and carrying a curved steel sword at his left hip.

bhanu_deva_iii_and_firuz_shah_tughlaq.figure: Bhanu Deva III and Firuz Shah Tughlaq
bhanu_deva_iii_and_firuz_shah_tughlaq.ref_desc: Bhanu Deva III has an oval medium-brown face, short black hair under a gold turban, cream tunic, deep red dhoti, dark green shawl, simple gold ornaments, brown sandals, and a dark red-hilt Odia sword in a brown scabbard, with a thoughtful worried expression.

narasimhadeva_i_and_the_konark_sthapatis.figure: Narasimhadeva I and the Konark sthapatis
narasimhadeva_i_and_the_konark_sthapatis.ref_desc: Narasimhadeva I has an oval medium-brown face, low-knotted black hair under a sun-emblem gold circlet, deep-red dhoti, golden-yellow angarkha, dark green uttariya and sheathed bronze-hilt sword, flanked by two off-white-dhoti sthapatis with blue and ochre shawls and bamboo measuring rod.

the_architects_of_konark.ref_desc: Shilpa-Surya is a lean, medium-brown Odia architect with an oval face, knotted black hair and headband, saffron tunic, cream dhoti, green shawl, simple sandals, copper studs, carrying a notched wooden measuring rod and rolled palm-leaf manuscript in saffron, cream and green tones.

the_jagannath_sevayats_and_maharis.ref_desc: A mid-20s Odia sevayat with off-white dhoti and angavastra, tulsi beads, knot-tied black hair and a cream Kenduli cloth beside a mid-20s Odia Mahari in deep crimson and mustard-gold Odia sari, jasmine-adorned bun, gold jewellery, Odissi mudra, in warm off-white, crimson and gold tones.

the_jagannath_temple_economy.ref_desc: A lean early-30s Odia man with an off-white turban, palm-leaf manuscript and stylus, off-white angarakha, deep-indigo dhoti with red border, mustard-yellow shawl, cowrie pouch, and brown sandals in a calm, thoughtful pose using off-white, deep indigo, mustard yellow, deep red, and brown.

eastern_ganga_administrators_and_mint_ma.figure: Eastern Ganga administrators and mint masters
eastern_ganga_administrators_and_mint_ma.ref_desc: A mid-30s Odia mint master with an oval medium-brown face, low knotted black hair under an off-white headband, off-white shawl, cream upper cloth, turmeric-yellow dhoti with maroon border, maroon waist sash, wooden beads, copper bangle, holding palm-leaf bundle and gold fanam coin in off-white, cream, yellow and maroon tones.

sarala_das.ref_desc: Sarala Das appears as a sturdy early‑forties Odia man with an oval medium‑brown face, small bun and off‑white headband, in an off‑white tunic, cream dhoti, turmeric‑yellow shawl and sandals, carrying a palm‑leaf manuscript and reed stylus in warm cream and maroon tones.

manavikrama_zamorin.ref_desc: Manavikrama Zamorin is a medium-brown, sharp-eyed man in off-white Kerala drapery with maroon and gold borders, black hair in a low knot under a narrow headcloth, simple gold ornaments, leather sandals, and a gleaming urumi sword with dark red-wrapped hilt.

ibn_battuta.ref_desc: Ibn Battuta is a mid-30s olive-brown Maghrebi traveler with a short beard, white turban, cream tunic, deep-indigo sleeveless robe, sand-beige trousers, brown slippers, rust-red sash, and a rolled parchment travel map in hand, using a cream and indigo-dominated palette.

zheng_he_and_ma_huan.ref_desc: Zheng He is a tall, broad-shouldered Ming admiral with a square-faced calm expression, black hair in a topknot under a dark-blue official hat, indigo naval robe with bird rank badge, red belt, black boots, and a rolled nautical chart in indigo, cream, red, black, and muted gold tones.

the_zamorin_s_merchant_council.ref_desc: A medium-brown Mappila merchant-councillor in a white cap with cream turban band, off-white kurta, cream mundu with dark green border, indigo waistcoat, brown sandals, green shoulder shawl, carrying a rolled palm-leaf document with red cord and brass seal.

calicut_pepper_merchants.ref_desc: Calicut Pepper Merchant has a warm brown oval face with short beard, shoulder‑length black hair under a dark indigo turban, off‑white angarkha, deep brown dhoti, brick‑red sash, palm‑leaf pepper basket with tally stick, and gold accents in a warm brown‑and‑indigo palette.

beypore_shipwrights.ref_desc: A mid-40s Beypore shipwright with medium brown skin, tied-back black hair and headband, in off-white mundu with maroon border and beige angarkha tunic, carrying a dark-brown wooden batten, with a brown leather belt and wooden wrist beads in a warm earthy palette.

zainuddin_makhdoom_ii_and_ezhuthachan.ref_desc: Zainuddin Makhdoom II is a thoughtful, medium-brown Malabar scholar in a white turban, white tunic, off-white dhoti, cream shawl, simple sandals and silver ring, carrying a narrow palm-leaf manuscript bundle in warm white, cream, brown and black tones.

vasco_da_gama_and_the_zamorin.figure: Vasco da Gama and the Zamorin
